summary: E passes: CLAIMS.md:100 [shelf] wh5ds names this exact stack as its reopen, and board/blob are unmoved (1.6904, 315119e2). The kernels transfer: decode's v4x module hash okc_campaign_engine_a_v4x_5a6b0753a8 and its ea6 regs equal moe's. Proceed only with two fixes. (1) Size: decode is already stripped, so strip_comments frees ~2 KB against a ~1,011 KB build; ~13 KB of real Python trimming is needed. (2) Picks: moe's '<= 0.98 every round through kernel_fn' bar was set on an expert-only kernel_fn. Decode's kernel_fn is the whole layer, which dilutes the gain, so pick on the isolated Engine A pair and use the layer only as a veto.
justification: A. The mechanism holds. E4/E5 change only the dequant instruction form and are bit-exact, and moe's judge run measured E/m per class on the same kernel bytes (702f1004 log: T1 E4/E4 .967, T8 .960, T16 .953, T32 .951, T128 E5 .955, T256 E4 .974 with cold iso .960; regs 82/83 and 64-70, lmem 0). Decode runs the same classes: T=1 v6pe2 (FAST), T=8 v4xs, T=32 v4cxs, and the cold half v4cxs at both T=128 and T=256. The board's 7cc034f9 log reads 'cold half ... T128 v4cx ... S | T256 v4cx ... S', and its v4x module hash equals moe's. Every moe anchor that _eae_src4x/_eae_src6 str.replace targets occurs with the same count in decode's source, so the CUDA port is mechanical. Two transfer gaps remain. (a) moe's T=128 was a plain Engine A route, not a hybrid: moe's _eae_base returns 'hybrid route' for T != 256, and moe's cold-half key is state['hm']['cold_x'][T]. Decode's T=128 and T=256 are H-16 hybrids that key state['hc']['cold_x'] by _hc_class, so the T=128 cold-half E path, and the T=256 one through hc, is new decode code that no run has exercised. moe's T=128 E5 .955 is a whole-block ratio and does not carry over; the right prior is moe's T=256 pattern (cold iso .960 -> kernel_fn .974). (b) Dilution, the WEAKEST LINK. moe's kernel_fn is the expert block. Decode's is the whole layer, with the expert block at 41-64% of the row. Projected layer E/m: T=1 ~.979, T=8 (verify_1) ~.983, T=16 ~.971, T=32 ~.975, T=128/256 cold-only ~.985-.99. Under a copied '<= 0.98 in every round' layer bar, T=8, T=128, T=256 and probably T=1 fall back to master. The stack would then deliver ~1% rather than 2.8%. Value estimate with per-row shares: E ~+1.8% headline if every class routes, plus wh5ds ~+0.4-0.8%. 35cc220c read +0.38% with T=16 on d, against a board that drew s. Total ~2.2-2.8%, so the 2.5% bar is reachable but not assured. Note that moe's own check overstated: +4.55% on the check, +2.29% on the scored run. Prior is correct: the earlier decode run (35cc220c) carried only wh5ds, and this adds a different mechanism. There is no do-not-retry overlap. T=16 pin: in the board's scored 7cc034f9, T=16 drew s ('16:s>d S1.016 pooled near 6r f2'). Its check 26435509, 44f30364 and 35cc220c drew d, and the layer race is a tie (d 171.4 vs s 171.6 us). The pin is also a prerequisite: E mirrors only s twins (moe _eae_base rejects EA4X_ARMS & 256), so with d drawn T=16 gets no E. The pin is wise. Pin the exact arm the board routed (v4xs or v4cxs, from 7cc034f9's [ead4x] lines), and update EAD4X_BOARD[16] from the stale 'd' to 's' so the '(board s/d/s)' print stops misleading.
confounders: hothalf-wh5ds (CLAIMS.md:100, branch hothalf-wh5ds-moe-port): at T=128 the hot-half cut 'hides under the cold half' (LOG 2582), so E-cold and wh5ds interact super-additively. Neither alone shows its true effect. Run the E race AFTER _wh_phase has routed wh5ds; that is moe's order, where [ea-enc] came after [hh-wh]. Otherwise the T=128/256 E ratios are measured on the wrong hot half. wh5ds's veto gate ran with master cold and must not be reused as evidence for E.
H-16 hybrid pins (CLAIMS.md:69, HC_PIN {128:-16, 256:-16}): H was tuned at master cold speed. A faster cold half may favour another H, so any gain is understated, but the A/B stays valid.
v6 fork guard and the side stream (CLAIMS.md:95): the cold half runs forked at priority 0. Time the E race at T=128/256 in fork mode, as judged, with serial as a second veto, as the wh5ds gate did.

v4c pinned at T=9..16 (CLAIMS.md:83): 'the layer prefers v4c though v4's block is 1.8-2.5% faster in isolation'. Isolated-pair ratios do not map 1:1 to the layer at T=16, which is why an isolated pick still needs a layer veto.
L3/L4 paired-scale decode (CLAIMS.md:74, :78): E4 keeps it and E5 replaces it. Both are raced against master in-run and are bit-exact, so this does not confound the result.
v4x-routes pooled hysteresis race (CLAIMS.md:95): the T=16 pin overrides it at T=16 only. T=8 and T=32 keep the race, and E mirrors whatever s twin they draw (both drew s in all four logs read).
interference: No companion is warranted. Each sub-change has an in-run control. E is raced per class against master with exactness gates, and the [ea-enc] ratios attribute it. wh5ds has its own isolated-pair pick and layer veto, and 35cc220c (1.6968, T=16 on d) is a wh5ds-alone judged control on the same base. The T=16 pin is deterministic and its effect shows in the [ea4x-dl] route line. A gain decomposes by class from the prints. A flat result with E routed reads as 'the H200 layer does not surface it'. A flat result with E unrouted reads as the bar or dilution problem above, so the prints must carry both the iso and the layer ratios. A revert of any landed hypothesis would answer nothing this run needs.
rules_flags: None blocking. E4/E5 are lossless prepare-time repacks: a code permutation, plus 7-bit scale fields only when every scale byte is in [0x08,0x7E]. Both are bit-exact to master and dequantized in-kernel.
The T=16 pin is a static, shape-only route set in prepare. It is legal, and it makes the final held-out rerun deterministic for that class.

Routes must be keyed only on shape and on prepare-time values. The hc cold_e must be keyed the same way as cold_x (by _hc_class) or on exact T. If it is keyed by class, run a canary at two non-judged T per class (e.g. 160 and 200), because the race measures only 128 and 256.

All syncs, the scale scan and the recode stay in prepare. kernel_fn adds only dict lookups and launches. Free the unrouted E copies (~906 MB each) and the wh copies, given decode's 80k-context KV footprint.
Size cap 1,000,000 B. strip_comments cannot get under it (see open_questions); any trimming must keep every CUDA string byte-identical (AST string-constant equality vs master).
freshness: E passes. CLAIMS.md:100 [shelf] wh5ds: its reopen is 'ride in the 10-30 decode stack (Engine A A4b/A5b encodings + T=16 ea4x pinned to s), aiming >= 2.5%', which is exactly this hypothesis, and the projected stack is ~2.2-2.8% (borderline). CLAIMS.md:93 and :95 [landed] v4x routes and v4xd-stack own these rows, and this builds on them (base blob 315119e2), not on a superseded base. CLAIMS.md:90 [lead] and :103 [unresolved, routing tail] are not touched by a bit-exact expert change. No decode claim is refuted or superseded for Engine A encodings; moe's version is landed (24f183ff 2.0201). Board: BEST 1.6904 (7cc034f9), master blob 315119e2, both unchanged since mint (0.00% vs a 1.24% margin), so it is fresh.
open_questions: SIZE (blocking for the build). decode master 955,413 B carries 177 comment chars and no docstrings: it is already stripped. The wh5ds branch is 988,094 B (~986,000 after stripping). moe's E delta after stripping is ~23.7 KB (948,099 vs 924,399, tokenize estimate). The decode hc-cold plumbing adds ~1-2 KB. That projects ~1,011,000-1,013,000 B, so ~13-15 KB must go. The hypothesis's 'strip_comments if needed' frees ~2 KB. Trim Python only, keep CUDA strings byte-identical, and prefer prepare-only race and diagnostic code of settled lanes. Candidates: wh5ds race arms D0/a3/wh, racing wh5ds vs m only while the module text stays identical; the [ea6-dl] inc(v1)-vs-v6 bench lines; superseded W6-G confirm-race code under HC_PIN; profiler and canary-only paths of b12p/c320d; moe-only branches in the E port such as Engine B/es1a checks, since decode has no EB_*. Run AST string-constant equality against master and report wc -c.

RACE BAR. Pick each class on the isolated Engine A pair: K1+K2 graph at T=1/8/16/32, and the cold pair at T=128/256 forked against the routed wh5ds hot half, at <= 0.98 every round. Then require a layer kernel_fn veto (<= 1.00 every round; fork and serial at T=128/256). A copied whole-layer 0.98 bar would reject most classes. At T=1 restrict the 8 K1xK2 combos to m/m, E4/E4, E5/E5 and E4/m, which cuts false picks and race time.

BUILD/PREPARE BUDGET. In 35cc220c, ea6-dl took 38.6 s, ea4x-dl 39.1 s and hh-wh 45 s in the background, the routes finished at 68 s, and prepare ended ~125 s. moe's two E modules took ~51 s each from t=0 with contention, and its race took 1.8 s. Expected decode end ~140-155 s with three extra background nvcc builds (eaenc-4x, eaenc-6, hh-wh). Watch for contention pushing ea6-dl/ea4x-dl past their own windows (EAD4X_START_S 90, EAD4X_GATE_S 100, EAD4X_CHECK_S 108; the v4x routes finished at ~68 s in 35cc220c). Start the E threads at t=0 but at lower priority (os.nice in the thread is not available, so consider starting them after ea4x-dl joins at ~68 s; they would still finish by ~125 s). Keep a hard EAE join deadline (moe 220 s) and the 255 s end, with master on timeout.

WHAT THE BUILD MUST PRINT, as the last ~2.5 KB of prepare. The log tail holds ~14 KB and 35cc220c's was already cut at the head (111 lines, 14,044 B). Required lines: [ea-enc] build s per module, join wait, phase-at; regs/lmem/occ per E instance; recode MB; scale scan and E5 eligibility; per T (1 with K1/K2, 8, 16, 32, 128, 256): exact y/n, iso E/m median[min,max], layer E/m per round (s and f at 128/256); PATH CHOSEN per T with the fallback reason. Reprint [hh-wh] ROUTE, GATE and PATH, stating that the E race ran after wh5ds was routed. Reprint [ea4x-dl] route with '16:s PIN <arm>' and the cold-half line. Reprint [hotcold] PATH T=128/256 condensed. End with the final 'prepare at X s'. Drop [hh-wh] ATTRS/SCALES (the moe check proved them) to make room.
Which s arm did 7cc034f9 route at T=16, v4xs or v4cxs? The pooled race spans EAD4X_RACE (v4xd, v4cxd, v4xs, v4cxs), and CLAIMS.md:83 pinned v4c at T=9..16. Pin exactly the board's arm.

Expected per-row reading: the largest E effect should show on decode_16 and decode_32 sliding (~2.4-2.9%), and the smallest on full verify rows (~1%). If verify_16/32 gain more than ~2%, credit the wh5ds+E-cold critical-path interaction, not E alone.
